scenes.name: warm and cold, as a count
scenes.visual: One continuous shot in two tiers. Upper tier: two to-scale bars of the same 1,032-token prompt, each 1,400 px wide, stacked at y≈260 and y≈400, row labels at the left 'a minute later' and 'a day later'. A cloud-and-sun icon sits top-left throughout; its label 'the weather conversation' shows during b1 only. In b3 the camera tilts down to the lower tier while the bars stay in view, dimmed, in the top band, and the G P U package draws at the right (compute die, H B M stacks outlined coral). In b4 a database cylinder icon draws at the left and an amber gear 'prefill' between them. The idea: warm and cold are two lengths of amber, and the difference is whether your blocks are still in the G P U's memory. Colour code for the whole chapter: keys and values themselves are coral tiles marked 'K V', exactly as in the previous chapter; teal = already held, a cache hit (a teal fill on token bars and pills, a teal outline and glow on K V tiles); amber = tokens that must be prefilled; blue = arriving tokens and neutral structure; coral = the G P U's memory and the K V tiles in it; grey dashed outline = nothing held, or evicted; solid grey = other people's blocks.

beats.say: Warm and cold are counts, not moods. A minute later, the weather conversation's follow-up brought one thousand and thirty-two tokens, all but five already cached. That is warm.
beats.show: Centre: a thermometer icon tagged 'warm / cold'; on 'counts, not moods', it morphs into a numeric counter and slides away. The cloud-and-sun icon settles top-left with its label 'the weather conversation', which fades as the beat ends. Upper bar: on 'one thousand and thirty-two tokens', an empty outline grows to 1,400 px with a counter at its right end, '1,032 tokens'. On 'all but five', it fills teal from the left for 1,027 units, label '1,027 held'; the last 5 units, a 7 px sliver, fill amber with a pointer 'prefill 5'. On 'That is warm', the row label gains a teal suffix: 'a minute later · warm'.

beats.say: A day later, in the coldest case, nothing is cached: all one thousand and thirty-two are prefilled, two hundred and six times the work.
beats.show: Lower bar: a grey dashed outline labelled '0 of 1,032 held'; on 'coldest case', the row label gains a grey suffix: 'a day later · cold'. On 'all one thousand and thirty-two', it fills amber left to right at an even pace, its label changes to 'prefill 1,032'. On 'two hundred and six', a plate between the rows: '1,032 ÷ 5 ≈ 206× the prefill work'. One small grey tag pops in at the right: 'same question, model, hardware'.

beats.say: The only difference is the cache, stored in fixed-size blocks, each holding keys and values for a few tokens. Warm, yours are still resident in the G P U's memory. Cold, they were evicted for someone else.
beats.show: On 'only difference', the grey tag 'same question, model, hardware' flashes once and fades. Camera tilts down; the bars and the plate shrink into the top band, and the bars' own labels fade, leaving the two row labels. The G P U package draws at the right. On 'fixed-size blocks', the teal part of the upper bar drops and breaks into six equal rounded coral tiles, each with a tiny 'K V' mark and a teal outline, label 'blocks', grey note 'schematic: a real chat fills many'. On 'resident', the tiles glide into the coral H B M stacks and their teal outlines glow, tag 'warm: still resident'. On 'evicted', solid grey blocks with tiny user icons slide in from the right and push yours out of the stacks; yours turn into grey dashed outlines, tag 'cold: evicted'.

beats.say: Only the small text survives, in a database. Your keys and values, the model's processed form of it, stopped existing. Rebuilding them from text is exactly what prefill does.
beats.show: On 'small text', the database cylinder draws at the left with a small blue document inside, tag 'text: small, kept'. On 'stopped existing', the dashed outlines in the H B M vanish. On 'Rebuilding', an arrow draws from the database through the amber 'prefill' gear into free slots in the H B M; the gear spins and coral K V tiles are rebuilt there one by one, each gaining a teal outline. Tag under the gear: 'text in, keys and values out'.

beats.say: So warm is a precise question. How many arriving tokens already have keys and values on this machine?
beats.show: Everything dims. Centre: a grey phrase 'a vague sense of readiness' writes on and is struck through; below it a plate writes on, 'how many arriving tokens are already held here?' A counter beside the plate flicks between '1,027' and '0'.

scenes.name: time t, the first question
scenes.visual: The case layout used in every case scene (s02 to s05, and again in s08): two rows in the upper middle, 'arriving' on top and 'in the cache' below, aligned token for token, row labels at the left. Segment widths are schematic, not to scale (corner note 'widths schematic'). The preamble is two segments, 'system' and 'tools', under a bracket 'shared preamble: 770'; question tokens are separate pills. Segments start blue and are coloured by state as the comparison runs. Below the rows, a result plate 'hit · prefill'. Top-right corner: a small scoreboard table with columns 'case', 'hit', 'prefill', which gains one row per case and stays through s05. Colours as in s01: teal held, amber prefilled, blue arriving or not yet decided, coral the G P U's memory and K V tiles, grey dashed nothing held or evicted.

beats.say: Now a smaller example, counted token by token. A service starts every conversation with the same preamble, system prompt and tools, seven hundred and seventy tokens.
beats.show: Top row draws on, label 'arriving': two blue segments 'system' and 'tools'. On 'every conversation', a faint stack of three ghost rows with the same two segments flickers behind and fades. On 'seven hundred and seventy', the bracket 'shared preamble: 770 tokens' draws under them. The empty scoreboard frame appears top right.

beats.say: At time t you ask, What is the capital of France? Seven tokens. Nothing in the cache matches, so all seven hundred and seventy-seven are prefilled.
beats.show: A clock icon tagged 'time t' appears above the row. Seven blue pills slide in after the preamble as spoken: 'What' 'is' 'the' 'capital' 'of' 'France' '?', bracket '7 tokens', sum at the row's right '770 + 7 = 777'. On 'Nothing in the cache matches', the bottom row draws as one grey dashed outline, label 'in the cache', text inside 'nothing that matches this conversation'. On 'all seven hundred and seventy-seven', the whole arriving row fills amber left to right; plate 'hit 0 · prefill all 777 tokens'; scoreboard row 'time t | 0 | 777'.

beats.say: The cold case, unavoidable the first time. Yet on a busy machine the preamble is probably cached already, leaving your seven tokens the only new work.
beats.show: Tag beside the plate: 'the expensive case: nothing reused'. On 'on a busy machine', faint grey user icons appear above the preamble; the preamble part of the cache row fills with teal hatching, tag 'probably cached by someone else'; the arriving 'system' and 'tools' change from solid amber to amber with teal hatching. On 'only new work', the seven question pills stay solid amber and pulse once, tag 'the only genuinely new work'.

scenes.name: case A, continue the chat
scenes.visual: Same case layout as s02, rebuilt. Arriving row: 'system', 'tools' and 'question 1' as compact segments, then seven pills for 'answer 1' and four pills for 'new'. A white vertical scan cursor runs along both rows for the front-to-back comparison. The scoreboard keeps its 'time t' row and gains 'A'. The idea: the cached prefix includes the model's own answer, so only the new words are new. Colours as in s01: teal held, amber prefilled, blue arriving or not yet decided, coral the G P U's memory and K V tiles, grey dashed nothing held or evicted.

beats.say: Case A: you continue the chat. The model answered, The capital of France is Paris. A minute later you add four new tokens. And its population?
beats.show: Label top-left: 'case A: continue the chat'. Arriving row rebuilds: 'system', 'tools', 'question 1', in blue. On 'The capital of France is Paris', seven blue pills slide in: 'The' 'capital' 'of' 'France' 'is' 'Paris' '.', bracket 'answer 1: 7'. On 'And its population', four pills: 'And' 'its' 'population' '?', bracket 'new: 4'. Sum at the right: '770 + 7 + 7 + 4 = 788'.

beats.say: That answer was cached as it was written, so everything before your new words matches. Hit, seven hundred and eighty-four. Prefill, four.
beats.show: Cache row builds: 'system', 'tools', 'question 1' in teal; on 'cached as it was written', the answer pills drop in one at a time, each clicking a small 'K | V' slab onto itself, tag 'cached as it was written'. On 'everything before', the scan cursor sweeps from the left; each arriving segment turns teal with a check as it passes; the cursor stops where the cache row ends, before 'new', marker 'first difference'. On 'Hit', the four new pills fill amber; plate 'hit 784 · prefill 4 tokens'; scoreboard row 'A | 784 | 4'.

beats.say: A perfect prefix, the model's own answer included. The best and most common case, and why a conversation stays quick while you keep typing.
beats.show: On 'own answer', the 'answer 1' pills in both rows glow teal together; line under the plate: 'a perfect prefix, answer included'. On 'keep typing', a small chat-window icon at bottom left shows short messages going back and forth; each adds only a short amber sliver to the end of a long teal bar beneath it, tag 'keep typing, stay warm'.

scenes.name: case B, one word changed
scenes.visual: Same case layout and orientation: 'arriving' on top, 'in the cache' below. The preamble collapses to one compact blue segment '770' in each row so the question pills can be large. In the cache: '770' then 'What' 'is' 'the' 'capital' 'of' 'France' '?'. Arriving: '770' then the new question, pill under pill. The white scan cursor returns. The scoreboard gains 'B'. Colours as in s01: teal held, amber prefilled, blue arriving or not yet decided, coral the G P U's memory and K V tiles, grey dashed nothing held or evicted.

beats.say: Case B, a minute later, a new conversation: What is the capital of Japan? The preamble and the first five words match, identical and in the same places.
beats.show: Label top-left: 'case B: a minute later, one word changed', and on 'new conversation' a small grey tag 'new conversation, not a follow-up'. The cache row shows the earlier question; the arriving pills slide in as spoken: 'What' 'is' 'the' 'capital' 'of' 'Japan' '?'. On 'The preamble', the cursor passes the two '770' segments and both turn teal. On 'first five words', each word pair turns teal with a check as the cursor passes it.

beats.say: Then France meets Japan, and the match ends. The question mark after it is redone too. Hit, seven hundred and seventy-five. Prefill, two.
beats.show: On 'France meets Japan', both pills flash and the cursor stops between 'of' and 'Japan'; marker 'diverges here'. On 'question mark', the two '?' pills glow and a thin link between them gets a small cross, tag 'same token, after the difference'. On 'Hit', 'Japan' and the arriving '?' fill amber; plate 'hit 775 · prefill 2 tokens'; scoreboard row 'B | 775 | 2'.

beats.say: A partial hit mid-sentence, which you could not arrange. Same-shaped questions start alike, and the rule never asks whose conversation, only whether tokens are identical from the front.
beats.show: On 'Same-shaped questions', faint ghost rows fan out behind from the shared start 'What is the capital of', ending in 'Spain ?', 'Peru ?', 'Kenya ?'; tag 'same shape, same start'. On 'whose conversation', the ghosts fade. On 'identical from the front', the five teal word pairs pulse once; line under the plate: 'identical from the front is all that counts'.

scenes.name: case C, the same words rearranged
scenes.visual: Same case layout and orientation as s04. In the cache: '770' then 'What' 'is' 'the' 'capital' 'of' 'France' '?'. Arriving: '770' then 'Tell' 'me' 'the' 'capital' 'of' 'France' 'please'. Grey arcs link the shared words between the rows. In b3 the cache row and plate fade, and case B's arriving row, compact, slides in above case C's for a side-by-side. The scoreboard gains 'C'. Colours as in s01: teal held, amber prefilled, blue arriving or not yet decided, coral the G P U's memory and K V tiles, grey dashed nothing held or evicted.

beats.say: Case C, the pair from earlier: Tell me the capital of France, please. It shares the whole phrase, the capital of France, but the very first token differs.
beats.show: Label top-left: 'case C: a minute later, same words reordered'. On 'the pair from earlier', a small grey tag 'seen earlier' flickers beside the label and fades. The arriving pills slide in as spoken. On 'the whole phrase', grey arcs draw between 'the', 'capital', 'of' and 'France' in the two rows, counter 'shared words: 4', and the four arcs glow together. On 'very first token', the cursor passes the '770' segments, turning them teal, and stops dead at the first pills; 'Tell' and 'What' flash, marker 'diverges at the very first token'; the arcs snap and fade.

beats.say: Only the shared preamble hits, seven hundred and seventy. All seven of your tokens are prefilled. Your words contributed nothing.
beats.show: All seven arriving pills fill amber. Plate 'hit 770 · prefill 7 tokens'; tag under the teal '770': 'shared preamble, nothing of yours'. Scoreboard row 'C | 770 | 7'.

beats.say: B and C are both seven tokens, like the original, sharing many of its words. Yet B matches five, C none, decided by which word came first.
beats.show: The cache row and plate fade. Case B's arriving row slides in above C's; each gets a bracket '7 tokens'. On 'matches five', B's first five pills glow teal with a badge '5 of 7'; on 'C none', C's pills stay amber with a badge '0 of 7'. On 'which word came first', the first pill of each row, 'What' and 'Tell', is circled. Line under the rows: 'which word came first decides'.

scenes.name: two ways to quote one hit rate
scenes.visual: The scoreboard flies from the corner to the centre and grows into a table with three rows, 'A continue the chat', 'B France to Japan', 'C same words, reordered'; its 'time t' row folds away for now (it returns in s08). Two value columns fill in turn: 'whole prompt' and 'your 7 tokens'. In b1 a to-scale bar of the 777-token prompt appears under the table and fades at the end of that beat. In b2 each cell of the second column holds a row of seven mini-pills and its fraction, so nothing sits beside the table. Idea: the same hits over two different totals tell opposite stories. Colours as in s01: teal held, amber prefilled, blue arriving or not yet decided, coral the G P U's memory and K V tiles, grey dashed nothing held or evicted.

beats.say: Against the whole prompt, all three hits look excellent, ninety-nine point one percent or better, because the preamble dominates and always matches.
beats.show: The scoreboard flies to the centre and becomes the table. Column 'whole prompt' fills in teal: 'A 784 / 788 = 99.5%', 'B 775 / 777 = 99.7%', 'C 770 / 777 = 99.1%'; on 'or better', a bracket spans the column, 'all above 99%'. On 'the preamble dominates', a to-scale bar of 777 units, 1,400 px wide, draws under the table: 770 units teal, 'preamble 770', and the last 7 units, a 13 px sliver, picked out with a pointer, 'your question: 7'. The bar fades as the beat ends.

beats.say: Count only your seven tokens. In case A, all seven matched, plus the whole history. Only four new words were fresh. B, five of seven. C, none.
beats.show: Column header 'your 7 tokens' appears. On 'In case A', A's cell: seven teal mini-pills and '7 / 7 · 100%'; on 'plus the whole history', a small teal tag inside the cell, 'plus the whole history'; on 'four new words', a second small tag inside the cell with four amber mini-pills, '+4 new, prefilled'. On 'five of seven', B's cell: five teal and two amber, '5 / 7 · 71%'. On 'none', C's cell: seven amber, '0 / 7 · 0%'.

beats.say: Same hits, opposite stories, decided by where the first divergence falls. The whole-prompt number flatters and hides the part you control, yet it is the one usually reported.
beats.show: On 'first divergence', a white marker slides into each pill row: after the 7th pill in A, after the 5th in B, before the 1st in C. On 'flatters', the 'whole prompt' column glows, tag 'usually reported'; the 'your 7 tokens' column gets the tag 'the part you control'. Line at the bottom: 'two ways to quote the same hits'.

scenes.name: a fixed pool, and pure pressure
scenes.visual: Centre: a wide coral-outlined panel, 'one machine's cache memory', filled with a schematic grid of equal blocks, about 6 rows by 14 columns (corner note 'schematic'). Blocks are coral K V tiles as in s01, with a teal outline while held. Your blocks are the three at the far left of the top row, with a small 'you' tag; they hold only your own conversation's history. A teal-outlined cluster at the left of the second row carries the tag 'shared preamble'. Every other block is solid grey with a tiny user icon: other people's. Each block shows a tiny clock dial for when it was last used. New requests arrive from the right as blue strips that need blocks. Evicted blocks turn grey dashed and drop out. In b3 the panel splits into a quiet and a busy machine, then merges; in b4 the camera pans right to a small schematic chart. Colours as in s01: teal held, amber prefilled, blue arriving or not yet decided, coral the G P U's memory and K V tiles, grey dashed nothing held or evicted.

beats.say: Why is a minute warm and a day cold? The cache is not a private locker but a fixed pool on one machine, and everyone competes for it.
beats.show: A locker icon with a padlock appears centre; on 'not a private locker', it gets a grey cross and fades. On 'fixed pool', the coral panel draws, label 'one machine's cache memory', and the grid fills row by row. Your three blocks light up, teal outlines glowing, with the 'you' tag; a sub-label in two lines under the panel: 'yours: the three on the left' / 'the rest: other people'. On 'everyone competes', blue request strips queue at the right edge.

beats.say: When a new request needs room, the least recently used blocks, untouched the longest, are dropped. Nothing is on a timer. It is pure pressure.
beats.show: Every block's clock dial becomes visible. A blue strip needing four blocks slides in from the right. On 'least recently used', the four blocks with the oldest dials turn grey dashed and drop out of the panel; the newcomer's blocks slide into their places. Tag 'least recently used goes first'. On 'Nothing is on a timer', a stopwatch icon gets a grey cross.

beats.say: A minute later, your blocks may survive on a quiet machine and be gone on a busy one. A day later, other people's conversations have flushed them everywhere.
beats.show: The panel duplicates into two side by side: left 'quiet machine', right 'busy machine', each with a plain grey label '1 minute later' (no stopwatch: nothing is on a timer). Left: an occasional strip trickles in and your three teal-outlined blocks survive. Right: a torrent of strips, the grid churns, and your blocks go grey dashed and vanish. On 'A day later', the panels merge; a sun-and-moon icon swings once across the top, label 'a day later', while the grid flickers through full refills, counter 'refilled ×1, ×2, ×3 …'; your blocks are nowhere. The shared-preamble cluster keeps a faint teal glow, unexplained until s08.

beats.say: Providers quote a lifetime of a few minutes, a guideline about typical load, not a guarantee. Eviction follows demand for space, not time: warmth is likely, not certain, and fades rather than expires.
beats.show: Camera pans right to a small chart marked 'schematic': x axis 'time since your last message', y axis 'chance your blocks are still there'. Two smoothly falling curves, a gentle one 'quiet machine' and a steep one 'busy machine'. On 'a few minutes', a dotted vertical line, 'quoted lifetime: a guideline'. On 'not time', a ghost step line, flat then dropping to zero at once, 'a timer: not how it works', gets a grey cross and fades. On 'fades rather than expires', the two curves glow; line beneath the chart: 'demand for space, not elapsed time'.

scenes.name: a day later, what survives
scenes.visual: Back to the case layout from s02: 'arriving' row on top, 'in the cache' row below, aligned token for token, row labels at the left, widths schematic, result plate under the rows, scoreboard in the top-right corner, rebuilt as in case A. The results table from s06 reappears at centre and shrinks back into the top-right scoreboard with all four rows, 'time t', 'A', 'B', 'C', and gains 'a day later'. A small database icon sits at the far left. In b2 the camera rises to a top band: nine user icons in a row, arrows down to one shared blue block. In b3 a small inset of the pool from s07 sits at bottom right. In b4 the camera pulls out to a router and three servers, then returns. Colours as in s01: teal held, amber prefilled, blue arriving or not yet decided, coral the G P U's memory and K V tiles, grey dashed nothing held or evicted.

beats.say: Now send case A's follow-up a day later. Your history was evicted overnight, so prefill rebuilds it from text.
beats.show: A day-night clock above the rows spins through 24 hours. The results table from s06 reappears at centre and shrinks back to the top-right scoreboard with all four rows: 'time t', 'A', 'B', 'C'. The arriving row rebuilds exactly as in case A: 'system', 'tools', 'question 1', 'answer 1', 'new', sum '788'. Cache row: 'system' and 'tools' in blue for now; 'question 1' and 'answer 1' as grey dashed outlines, text 'evicted overnight'. On 'prefill rebuilds it', the arriving 'question 1' and 'answer 1' turn amber and send copies down through a small amber 'prefill' gear that fill the dashed outlines. The database icon gets a tag 'the text was kept'.

beats.say: The preamble is different: the most shared text in the system. Its keys and values are computed once per machine and reused by every request.
beats.show: The cache row's 'system' and 'tools' turn solid teal. Camera rises to the top band: nine user icons appear one after another and arrows draw down from them to one blue block, 'the same system prompt, token for token'; header 'the most shared text in the system'. On 'computed once', an amber gear beside the block spins once, tag 'computed once per machine'. On 'reused by every request', each arrow pulses teal in turn into the teal preamble below, tag 'reused by every request'.

beats.say: Touched by thousands of conversations all day, it is almost never least recently used: the most reliable hit there is. Hit, seven hundred and seventy. Prefill, eighteen, against four a minute later.
beats.show: Camera returns to the rows. Bottom-right inset of the pool: the teal-outlined preamble blocks' clock dials keep resetting to 'just now' with each pulse while grey blocks age and drop; a grey eviction sweep passes and skips them. On 'thousands of conversations', tag 'kept warm by everyone else'. On 'Hit', the arriving 'system' and 'tools' turn teal; 'question 1', 'answer 1' and 'new' stay amber. Plate 'hit 770 · prefill 18 tokens', breakdown under the 18: '7 + 7 + 4'. On 'four a minute later', the scoreboard row 'a day later | 770 | 18' slides in directly under 'A | 784 | 4', and the 4 and the 18 glow.

beats.say: That only helps on the same machine, so the router sends each request where its prefix already sits.
beats.show: Camera pulls out: a request parcel at the left, a router icon at centre, three server icons at the right, the middle one glowing teal with the tag 'holds this prefix'. On 'sends each request', the parcel passes through the router to the glowing server; ghost paths to the other two fade. Tag at the router: 'route by prefix'.

beats.say: The preamble usually survives, kept warm because it is shared. Yours does not, because nobody else was keeping it alive.
beats.show: Camera returns to the rows. The teal preamble pulses with the crowd of user icons above it; the amber history segment stands alone with one greyed user icon above it. A ghost of s01's all-amber 'a day later' bar flashes beneath and gains a teal front section, tag 'the preamble usually survives'. Line under the plate: 'shared survives, yours does not'.

scenes.name: cheap because warm
scenes.visual: Left half: the shared blue block from s08 with its nine user icons and arrows above it, small, its keys and values shown as a row of coral K V tiles with teal outlines beneath it. Right half: a price comparison drawn to scale, then an illustrative bill for case C. Idea: being shared keeps it warm, and warm is what makes it cheap. Colours as in s01: teal held, amber prefilled, blue arriving or not yet decided, coral the G P U's memory and K V tiles, grey dashed nothing held or evicted.

beats.say: Warmth also makes a large fixed preamble cheap. A cached read, an input token already held, skips prefill, so it is cheap to serve. Providers price it at roughly a tenth of a fresh one.
beats.show: Right half: a price-tag icon. On 'a cached read', a teal token pill with the tag 'cached read: an input hit'. On 'skips prefill', a small amber gear icon beside the pill gets a grey cross. On 'cheap to serve', a tag on the shared block at the left: 'cheap to serve'. On 'a tenth', two bars to scale: 'fresh input token', amber, 400 px; 'cached input token', teal, 40 px, label 'about 1/10'.

beats.say: Illustratively, case C's seven hundred and seventy-seven input tokens would bill like about eighty-four fresh ones.
beats.show: Below the price bars, a small bill builds line by line: '770 cached × 0.1 = 77', then '+ 7 fresh = 84'. Beside it, two bars to scale, 777 units = 1,000 px: 108 px in teal, 'billed like 84', against 1,000 px in amber, 'all fresh: 777'. Grey footnote: 'illustrative; real discounts vary'.

beats.say: The preamble's warmth is not luck. It comes from being shared, and it is why cached input is priced separately.
beats.show: The bill fades. The nine arrows pulse teal into the shared block once more; header above it: 'the one block everybody shares'. Centred line at the bottom: 'warm because shared, cheap because warm'.

scenes.name: the expensive place to edit
scenes.visual: One long prompt row across the upper third: the first five token slots shown individually and numbered 1 to 5, then long blue segments 'rest of the system prompt', 'tools', 'everything after'. A white vertical marker 'the match ends here'. Mid-scene the camera pulls out to show this row as the top of a stack of conversation rows on one machine, all sharing the same front. At the end, a horizontal band from 'most stable' to 'most variable'. Colours as in s01: teal held, amber prefilled, blue arriving or not yet decided, coral the G P U's memory and K V tiles, grey dashed nothing held or evicted.

beats.say: Being shared also makes the preamble expensive to edit. Change one token at position five, and the match ends there. Nothing after it is reused, however identical.
beats.show: Header: 'Change one token at the very front'. The row draws. On 'position five', slot 5 flips from blue to amber with the label 'edit'. The scan cursor runs from the left: slots 1 to 4 turn teal, it stops at slot 5, and the marker drops: 'the match ends here'. On 'Nothing after it', the long segments turn amber from left to right, tag 'identical, but after the difference'.

beats.say: Every conversation on the machine shares that prefix, so all go cold at once. The weather conversation's next turn prefills one thousand and twenty-eight tokens, not five.
beats.show: Camera pulls out: the row becomes the top of a tall stack of conversation rows with different tails and the same front, a small user icon at each row's left. On 'at once', the white marker extends down through every row and everything to its right turns amber in one sweep. On 'weather conversation', one row tagged with the cloud-and-sun icon enlarges; beneath it two amber bars to scale, 1,028 units = 1,200 px: a 6 px sliver 'before the edit: 5' and a 1,200 px bar 'after: 1,028'.

beats.say: About two hundred and six times the prefill work, from one token. So operators edit a production system prompt with care.
beats.show: A plate under the bars: '1,028 ÷ 5 ≈ 206× the prefill work'. On 'with care', a warning-sign icon appears over the system-prompt part of the top row, tag 'edit with care'.

beats.say: Most stable text first, most variable last: the ordering you met earlier. Now you know what it protects.
beats.show: The stack fades. A horizontal band appears, deep teal at the left fading to amber at the right, labelled 'front: most stable' and 'back: most variable'. On 'Most stable text first', segments slot onto it in order: 'system prompt', 'tools', 'your conversation', 'newest message'. On 'what it protects', the teal front of the band glows and a line writes on beneath: 'order matters: stable first, variable last'.

checks.claim: CORRECTION: atlas figs 44 and 47 say 'warm: 906 of 911 already held, prefill 5'; the film uses Example A, 1,027 of 1,032, so the warm and cold rows describe the same 1,032-token conversation. Both leave 5 tokens to prefill and both round to a 99.5% hit.
Warm follow-up: 1,032 - 1,027 = 5 tokens to prefill ('all but five already held')
Cold vs warm prefill: 1,032 / 5 = 206.4, said 'two hundred and six times the prefill work', shown '1,032 ÷ 5 ≈ 206×'
s01 bars at 1,400 px for 1,032 tokens: the warm amber sliver is 5 units = 6.8 px, the teal part 1,027 units = 1,393 px
